;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[2020 Mogadishu army base bombing]]
***A [[suicide bombing]] at a [[military base]] in [[Mogadishu]] kills at least eight people and injures fourteen others. [[Jihadist]] group [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-blast/blast-rocks-military-base-in-somali-capital-at-least-eight-dead-idUSKCN2540E4 (Reuters)]
*[[2019–2020 Lebanese protests]], aftermath of the [[2020 Beirut explosions]]
**[[Riot police]] fire [[tear gas]] at protesters trying to make their way into [[Parliament of Lebanon|parliament]], amid increasing anger at the [[Government of Lebanon|government]]'s handling of this week's explosions in [[Beirut]] and deteriorating [[Economy of Lebanon|economic situation]] in the country. More than 728 people were wounded in the clashes, sixty-three of whom were taken to hospitals, while a [[Internal Security Forces|policeman]] was killed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/60-missing-beirut-mega-blast-live-updates-200808061240497.html (Al Jazeera)]
**Protesters storm the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants (Lebanon)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants]] building in [[Achrafieh]], Beirut. The building was badly damaged in the August 4 explosion. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-53704998 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**[[Mauritius]] declares a state of environmental emergency after the [[Japan]]ese-owned ship MV ''Wakashio'' ran aground offshore days ago and began spilling tons of fuel. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/07/world/africa/mauritius-oil-spill.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Bohumín arson attack]]
**A fire at a 13-story apartment complex in [[Bohumín]], [[Czech Republic]], kills eleven people and injures ten others. [[Rescue worker]]s say all of those who died resided on the 11th and 12th floors of the building, with five of them jumping from the windows "in a panic". [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/police-10-killed-apartment-fire-czech-republic-72257740 (ABC News)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Paris]] issues a mask mandate for busy areas to curb the rise of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] infections. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-paris-masks-idUSKCN2540QH (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports 174 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. This is the highest number of reported cases since early May. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-ireland/ireland-reports-highest-number-of-new-covid-19-cases-since-early-may-idUSKCN2540SU (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The total number of COVID-19 deaths in [[Brazil]] surpasses 100,000. [https://g1.globo.com/bemestar/coronavirus/noticia/2020/08/08/brasil-supera-100-mil-mortes-por-covid-19-segundo-consorcio-de-veiculos-de-imprensa.ghtml (G1)] [https://www.wsj.com/articles/brazil-faces-somber-covid-19-milestone-at-100-000-deaths-11596898801 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The United States surpasses five million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-usa-cases/u-s-sets-record-as-coronavirus-cases-top-5-million-idUSKCN2540XB (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[LGBT rights in Poland]]
**The [[Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe]] [[Dunja Mijatović]] urges Polish authorities to "immediately release" an [[LGBT rights]] activist detained on Friday. The activist was arrested on charges of [[hooliganism]] and [[vandalism]]. Yesterday, 48 pro-LGBT protesters were also arrested when they tried to stop [[policja (Poland)|police]] from detaining the activist. [https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/eu-commissioner-urges-poland-to-release-detained-lgbt-rights-activist-14707 (''The First News'')]
**Thousands of protesters march in front of the [[Palace of Culture and Science]] in [[Warsaw]], demanding the release of the activist. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-poland-lgbt/thousands-protest-in-poland-demanding-release-of-lgbt-activist-idUSKCN2540DM?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**On the eve of a [[2020 Belarusian presidential election|presidential election]], [[Belarus]]ian security forces arrest [[Maria Moroz]], the campaign manager of leading opposition candidate [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]], and three [[Open Russia]] activists who traveled to Belarus to "observe Sunday's presidential election".   [https://www.dw.com/en/belarus-police-arrest-activists-journalists-ahead-of-vote/a-54498508 (DW)]

;Sports
* [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
** The [[Mid-American Conference]] announces that its 12 members will not play this fall season, including in [[College football|football]]. While many other [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] leagues have already called off fall sports, the MAC becomes the first [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|Division I FBS]] league to scrap the [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2020 football season]]. [https://getsomemaction.com/news/2020/8/7/general-mid-american-conference-announces-postponement-of-fall-sports.aspx (Mid-American Conference)] [https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/29621025/source-mac-cancels-fall-football-season-eyes-move-spring (ESPN)] <!--The MAC is NOT the first NCAA league to call off its fall sports season. It's the first *FBS* league to do so.-->
